name: Conditional short-run emissions effect of shifting a flexible workload

treatment.description: Move an energy-conserving workload from the baseline start time to a candidate start time.

outcome.name: total_interconnected_grid_operational_emissions_delta
outcome.spatial_boundary: France and responding interconnected European bidding zones

target_population.eligibility: Flexible workloads that can move within the next 24 hours without violating user constraints

identified_estimator.model: Y = g(X) + T * m(X), with m(X) constrained nonnegative
identified_estimator.treatment_measure: observed actual workload energy in MWh at the executed start
identified_estimator.control_pool: unexecuted feasible candidate hours with no overlap with actual execution
identified_estimator.confidently_avoided_definition: max(0, lower 80% interval bound for avoided kgCO2e)
identified_estimator.identification_scope: observationally identified under the stated DAG assumptions after all readiness gates pass

dml_companion_estimator.role: parallel robustness estimator; it does not automatically replace the constrained estimator
dml_companion_estimator.nuisance_models: histogram gradient boosting for conditional outcome and continuous treatment
dml_companion_estimator.cross_fitting: rolling-origin decision blocks using only earlier observations and the same 24-hour embargo
dml_companion_estimator.comparison_policy: report effect-level agreement, correlation, and sign disagreement against constrained_marginal_response_v1

identification_assumptions: The adjustment set is measured before the workload decision.
No material common cause of workload timing and emissions remains unmeasured after adjustment.
Candidate workload timings have sufficient overlap in comparable pre-decision grid states.
The response horizon captures material dispatch, storage, balancing, and cross-border effects.
The estimated effect is valid only for workload sizes represented by the treatment definition or an explicitly validated size range.
